{"concepts_used":["GC-0040","GC-0097","GC-0128","GC-0046"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part51/2/2/4","quote":"Opposition to registration or protection"},{"ref":"TMM/Part51/2/2/4","quote":"If the extension was for filing evidence in reply, the period allowed for the parties to file their evidence concludes and the parties will have the opportunity to request a hearing."},{"ref":"TMM/Part51/5#1~1","quote":"Once the period for the parties to serve their evidence has ended the Registrar must decide the opposition"}],"answer":"For an opposition to registration or protection, the Manual’s practice is that, if an extension to file evidence in reply is refused:

- The period allowed for the parties to file evidence ends.
- The parties then have the opportunity to request a hearing. A hearing is not described as automatic. [TMM/Part51/2/2/4]

The Manual also states that, once the evidence period has ended, the Registrar must decide the opposition. This describes the next procedural stage, not who will succeed. [TMM/Part51/5#1~1]

These are statements of Manual practice, not quotations from legislation. The supplied Act and Regulations passages do not specify the consequences of this refusal, a deadline for requesting a hearing, or any review rights. If your opposition concerns removal or cessation of protection instead, the relevant evidence-in-reply passage is cut off, so I cannot confirm that procedure from the supplied text."}
